title: Fredrick
dek: An adventurer whose place in the grimoire’s custody history gives a seemingly unreadable possession consequences beyond his lifetime.

facts.Death: Recorded in legacy account; scene and date unrecovered

sources: Deep character dossier · supplied 14 October 2026; quest evidence takes precedence
Selected primary scenes and established public histories; anchors below
body:
Fredrick’s history includes travel, trading and the book that later becomes a crucial part of Papirak’s legacy. The record is fuller about what passed through his hands than about his complete life. That imbalance leaves questions to recover, rather than making him merely an unnamed step in an object’s history.

An adventurer among companions

In the Before expedition he examines old remains, prepares to travel with a borrowed blanket and trades with Aravil. These scenes place him among people acting on partial information. They do not establish that every arcane book in the expedition was Papirak’s grimoire.

The newcomer history also preserves Fredrick receiving practical help: food, orientation, maps, work information and personal support. That welcome belongs beside the later account of his possessions, without manufacturing a precise chronology between separately recorded scenes.

The book that outlives him

The established grimoire history traces the book from Papirak to Stash, then Fredrick, whose view of its pages is blank despite the inscription. After his death, the record places it among possessions taken by Ale-Chemy and later in their circulation.

Minerva finds no accessible spell record. Much later, Ryvyt uses Truesight with Jiangshi present and discovers hidden spells. That later discovery does not change what Fredrick could see. His observation is evidence of his experience, not proof that the book contained nothing.

Nor does the later identification mean he knowingly stole Papirak’s property or understood what he carried. Papirak’s own death is a separate event; the book had already moved into this custody history.

The unfinished personal history

Fredrick’s death scene, exact dates of the book’s transfers, the people present at the looting and the fate of his other possessions remain unrecovered here. No moral or legal verdict is assigned to the transfer without that context. The clue passes through other people’s hands after Fredrick; that later history does not show that he understood everything it would reveal.

Recorded scenes

Dates refer to transcript postings, not an independently established in-world calendar.

  • 17 April 2025 · the examined remains
  • Preparing to travel
  • 23 April · Aravil offers a book in trade
